First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={75}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({75}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {75}^{∘})=\operatorname{sin}⁡({150}^{∘})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}10\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({75}^{∘})\operatorname{csc}⁡({150}^{∘}) & =5\cdot [2\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({75}^{∘})]\operatorname{csc}⁡({150}^{∘}) \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡({150}^{∘})\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡({150}^{∘})} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
